mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the coefficient of variation (CV) for a data set?

options.A: CV = (Standard deviation ÷ Mean) × 100, expressed as a percentage.
options.B: CV = (Mean ÷ Standard deviation) × 100, expressed as a percentage.
options.D: CV = (Range ÷ Mean) × 100, expressed as a percentage.

mcqs.answer: CV = (Standard deviation ÷ Mean) × 100, expressed as a percentage.
mcqs.explanation: The coefficient of variation is defined as the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, multiplied by 100 to express it as a percentage. Option B reverses the ratio, C multiplies instead of dividing, and D uses the range, which is not part of the CV definition.

mcqs.question: For the data set {12, 15, 18, 21, 24}, what is the coefficient of variation (rounded to one decimal place)?
mcqs.explanation: Mean = (12+15+18+21+24)/5 = 18. Variance = [(−6)²+(−3)²+0²+3²+6²]/5 = 90/5 = 18, so SD = √18 ≈ 4.24. CV = (4.24/18)×100 ≈ 23.6%. The other options result from incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: Data set A has a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 5. Data set B has a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 12. Which data set is more consistent?

options.D: Consistency cannot be determined from the given information

mcqs.explanation: Consistency is measured by the coefficient of variation. CV_A = (5/50)×100 = 10%. CV_B = (12/80)×100 = 15%. The lower CV indicates greater consistency, so Data set A is more consistent. Options B, C, and D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: Two classes took the same exam. Class X: mean = 70, SD = 7. Class Y: mean = 70, SD = 14. Which statement best interprets the relative dispersion of the scores?

options.A: Class X has lower relative dispersion, indicating its scores are more tightly clustered around the mean.
options.B: Class Y has lower relative dispersion, indicating its scores are more tightly clustered around the mean.
options.C: Both classes have the same relative dispersion because their means are equal.
options.D: Relative dispersion cannot be compared without knowing the range of scores.

mcqs.answer: Class X has lower relative dispersion, indicating its scores are more tightly clustered around the mean.
mcqs.explanation: Relative dispersion is measured by the coefficient of variation. CV_X = (7/70)×100 = 10%; CV_Y = (14/70)×100 = 20%. A lower CV means less relative spread, so Class X is more consistent. Options B, C, and D ignore the role of standard deviation in CV.

mcqs.question: The coefficient of variation (CV) is:

options.A: (Standard deviation ÷ Mean) × 100, expressed as a percentage.
options.B: (Mean ÷ Standard deviation) × 100, expressed as a percentage.

mcqs.answer: (Standard deviation ÷ Mean) × 100, expressed as a percentage.
mcqs.explanation: CV is defined as the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, multiplied by 100. This makes it a dimension‑less measure of relative variability. The other options misuse the formula.

mcqs.question: Find the coefficient of variation for the data set {5, 7, 9, 11, 13} (rounded to one decimal place).
mcqs.explanation: Mean = (5+7+9+11+13)/5 = 9. Variance = [(−4)²+(−2)²+0²+2²+4²]/5 = 40/5 = 8, so SD = √8 ≈ 2.83. CV = (2.83/9)×100 ≈ 31.4%. The other options arise from incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: When comparing two data sets using the coefficient of variation, which statement is correct?

options.A: The data set with the lower CV is more consistent.
options.B: The data set with the higher CV is more consistent.
options.C: CV does not provide any information about consistency.
options.D: Consistency can be judged only by looking at the standard deviation.

mcqs.answer: The data set with the lower CV is more consistent.
mcqs.explanation: A lower coefficient of variation indicates that the spread of the data is small relative to its mean, meaning the data are more consistent. Options B and C contradict the definition of CV, and D ignores the relative nature of CV.

mcqs.question: A snack company packs two products. Product A: mean weight = 500 g, SD = 5 g. Product B: mean weight = 200 g, SD = 5 g. Which product shows greater relative dispersion?

options.C: Both have the same relative dispersion
options.D: Cannot be determined without the range

mcqs.explanation: CV_A = (5/500)×100 = 1%. CV_B = (5/200)×100 = 2.5%. The higher CV for Product B indicates greater relative dispersion. Option B reverses the comparison, C ignores the difference, and D is unnecessary because CV already accounts for relative spread.
